questions.q: What does the New Year’s message say happened to the lessons of the pandemic?

Yes. The message calls us back to it.

Not quite. The article says: The gratitude people felt for simple blessings faded once the crisis passed.

Not quite. The article says: The gratitude people felt for simple blessings faded once the crisis passed.

questions.q: The Prophet likened himself to “a rider who stops under the shade of a tree for a while and then moves on.” What does the message draw from this?
options: Avoid owning anything at all
Not quite. The article says: Take from the world only what the journey needs, without becoming attached to possessions.
Rest more than you work
Not quite. The article says: Take from the world only what the journey needs, without becoming attached to possessions.
Take from the world only what the journey needs, without becoming attached to possessions
Right. Life here is brief.
Travel as often as possible
Not quite. The article says: Take from the world only what the journey needs, without becoming attached to possessions.
questions.rationale: “This Hadith encourages us to take only what we need for life’s journey and to avoid becoming overly attached to worldly possessions.”

options: It produces nothing
Not quite. The article says: It works in perfect order yet carries no labels or guides – its message is silent, and faith and inquiry help us read it.

Not quite. The article says: It works in perfect order yet carries no labels or guides – its message is silent, and faith and inquiry help us read it.

Yes. Design points to a Designer.

questions.article: The Power of Quality in Today’s World
questions.q: After his shop caught fire, a shopkeeper restocked and put up the sign “You will find everything fresh in this shop.” What does the story illustrate?
options: Fires are good for business
Not quite. The article says: Positive thinking turns a setback into an opportunity.
Advertising is dishonest
Not quite. The article says: Positive thinking turns a setback into an opportunity.
Positive thinking turns a setback into an opportunity
Well read. There are more possibilities than problems.
Losses should be hidden
Not quite. The article says: Positive thinking turns a setback into an opportunity.
questions.rationale: “The shopkeeper’s choice to focus on opportunity rather than loss not only restored his business but elevated it to new heights.”
